text:
Mira: seeing repeated p95/p99 latency spikes on shared-gpu pool 'zeta' starting ~00:15 UTC. correlated with a handful of users sending long-sequence batches (seq_len=8192) interleaved with short chats. p50 fine, but tail jumps by ~600ms for ~6m windows.

Jon: is this the noisy tenant we saw last week? any kernel switches in the logs?

Mira: looks like it. kernel_autoswitch logs show a bunch of churn:
```
2026-03-17T00:14:58Z kernel_switch: model=redwood-v2-finetune conv_attn_fuse_v2 -> conv_attn_fallback reason=kv-slot-pressure
2026-03-17T00:14:59Z kv_eviction: tenant=T-127 slots=42 total_slots=2048
2026-03-17T00:15:05Z kernel_switch: conv_attn_fallback -> conv_attn_fuse_v2 reason=latency_regain
```
churn aligns with the tail. hypothesis: long-seq batches thrash KV slots, autoswitch flips kernels (fallback has different perf characteristics) and we pay context-restore/compile warmup.

Alex: ugh. Do we have per-tenant KV slot accounting turned on?

Mira: yes but we only expose aggregate counts. During the spike: kv_evictions per-tenant peaked ~1200/5m for T-127 while other tenants stayed <20.

Sam: did batching heuristics amplify this? long-seq requests can cause big batch variance. I remember a setting that extends batch window if it expects more tokens. If a long job lands, it increases batch size and delays small requests — could explain p99 bump.

Kevin: got profiling traces for one affected GPU (gpu-zeta-12). attaching condensed flame: conv_attn_fallback spends more time in memory copies and does an extra KV sync on start, so each kernel flip costs ~120ms. Repro pattern: interleaved long-short requests within 200ms of each other.

Mira: repro script I used (internal):
```bash
# repro: generate interleaved load
python tools/loadgen/interleave.py --target pool=zeta --tenant T-127 --long-len 8192 --short-len 128 --rps-long 2 --rps-short 50 --duration 300
```
results: p99 went from 210ms -> 820ms during repro. kv_evictions and kernel_switch count rose correspondingly.

Jon: quick mitigation options?

Alex: short-term: apply tenant soft-lease cap for T-127 to limit concurrent long seq workers (cap to 2). Also enable kv-slot-quota per-tenant (soft) to prevent single tenant starving slots. That should cut eviction churn.

Tara: can we tune kernel_autoswitch hysteresis? e.g. require 3 consecutive samples before flip or set cooldown to 30s. That reduces flip-thrashing but may delay a beneficial switch.

Sam: batching tweak: reduce adaptive batch max_latency from 50ms -> 20ms for pool zeta for the next 2 hours to favor latency for small requests. Might raise cost but lowers p99.

Mira: agree. Proposed immediate runbook:
1) Apply tenant soft-lease cap T-127 (owner: Alex)
2) Enable per-tenant kv-slot soft-quota (owner: Kevin)
3) Deploy kernel_autoswitch cooldown = 30s on pool zeta (owner: Jon)
4) Reduce adaptive batch max_latency to 20ms for pool zeta (owner: Sam)
5) Run the repro for 10m and collect traces + kv metrics (owner: Mira)

Kevin: I'll flip the kv-slot-quota flag now in canary (zeta-11). CI bot triggered a canary deploy: 
ci-bot: started deploy job #4823 -> canary zeta-11

ci-bot: deploy #4823 passed smoke checks on zeta-11 at 00:47 UTC

Alex: soft-lease cap applied to tenant T-127 at 00:49 UTC (reduced concurrent long workers from 8 -> 2). Monitoring now.

Sam: batch max_latency override applied at 00:50 UTC for pool zeta.

Mira: running repro now for 10m. initial run shows p99 dropped from ~820ms to ~260ms during the same load. kv_evictions dropped to ~18/5m for T-127. kernel_switch events reduced by ~85%.

Jon: nice. Longer-term we should:
- implement per-tenant sequence-length heatmap for smarter routing (send long-seq to dedicated lanes)
- consider slot pinning for active KV sets to avoid eviction storms
- evaluate more graceful kernel transition (background compile)

Tara: adding a ticket for the longer-term items and scheduling a deep-dive with runtime + scheduler next week.

Mira: thanks all, will keep monitoring overnight and escalate if anything reappears. :thumbsup:
